names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 4 iulie, «Sfântul Ierarh Andrei Criteanul, Arhiepiscopul Cretei».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 4 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Ανδρέας ο Ιεροσολυμίτης Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κρήτης», with the rank words and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 4. јул ст. ст., „Св. Андреј архиеп. Критски“ — Св. is not a rank, „архиеп.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries, and „Критски“ is the see that rank governs and comes off with it, as the folder’s own Greek form was taken «with the rank words and the see left off» and as „Московски“, „Јерусалимски“ and „Цариградски“ came off Photius, Juvenal and Anatolius earlier in this range. **The fold that leaves is four deep and one of its members is a second Cretan Andrew, which is this day’s reading for the author to weigh**: `foldchk.py` returns `andrew-companion-of-paul`, `andrew-the-monk-martyr-of-crete` and `andrew-the-presbyter-confessor`, all `sr`, for «Андреј», and NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Андреј Критски». So keeping the see would have avoided the fold **and** would have told the two Cretan Andrews apart; it was still refused, because the see governs the rank and the rule strips it, and because this folder’s other two forms were taken the same way. Measured, not supposed, and said plainly rather than quietly settled.

death.note: Two books, two years twenty-eight apart, and the field is widened rather than chosen. saint.gr, as this folder’s life already had it: «he died in 740 aboard ship on the way back from Constantinople», buried at Eresos on Lesbos. The Охридски пролог for 4. јул ст. ст.: „Када лађа пловљаше близу острва Митилене, сконча свој земни живот овај светилник цркве и пресели се душом у царство Христово 712 г.“ — the ship sailing near the island of Mitylene, in the year 712. doxologia names his parents and the place of his death and gives no year at all. **712 is also the year saint.gr gives for the synod Philippikos Bardanes convoked and Andrew took part in**; reading this book’s year of death as that page’s year of a synod would be choosing between the two books on a guess, and it is recorded here and nowhere acted on. The year 681 of the Sixth Ecumenical Council, which this book gives, is a Council’s year and not his, and no field takes it; nothing is reckoned from it (5 October 2026).

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 4 July is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **A WIDENED DATE, TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS APART, AND A COINCIDENCE IN THE NUMBERS THAT IS RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON.** The folder held `death` 740 to 740 off saint.gr: «he died in 740 aboard ship on the way back from Constantinople». doxologia names his parents and the place of death and gives no year at all. This book ends „сконча свој земни живот овај светилник цркве и пресели се душом у царство Христово 712 г.“ — in the year 712. The rule widens and does not choose: `death` earliest 712, latest 740, display «712 or 740», basis traditional, both sentences in the note. **And the coincidence**: 712 is also the year saint.gr gives for the synod Philippikos Bardanes convoked, which that page says Andrew took part in. Reading this book’s year of death as the other book’s year of a synod would be choosing between them on a guess, and it is written in the note and nowhere acted on — the same shape as Photius’s 1430 standing beside the Russian life’s angel of 20 April 1430 on 2 July. **THE 681 OF THE SIXTH COUNCIL IS NOT A DATE OF HIS AND NO FIELD TAKES IT.** „сабра се у Цариграду шести Васељенски Сабор 681 год. у време царовања Константина Брадатог“ — the Sixth Ecumenical Council gathered at Constantinople in 681 in the reign of Constantine the Bearded. A Council is not a folder and a Council’s year is not a man’s; the folder holds no `birth` and no `floruit` before this day and holds neither after it. **Nothing is reckoned** from 681 and 712 together, nor from 681 and 740, and the emperor is no source for a year. WHAT IS NEW, AND IT IS THE WHOLE MIDDLE OF HIS LIFE. The folder had the dumbness until seven and the loosing of his tongue at communion, the schooling, the episcopal charity and the death at Eressos. This book adds: that at fourteen he went to Jerusalem and was tonsured in the lavra of Sabbas the Sanctified, surpassing in understanding and ascesis many older monks; that the patriarch then took him for his own secretary; that when the **monothelite** heresy began to rage — „која учаше да Господ Исус немаше вољу човечанску него само вољу божанску“ — the Sixth Council met, and that **Theodore patriarch of Jerusalem, unable to go himself, sent Andrew, then archdeacon, as his plenipotentiary**, where he showed his gift, his eloquence, his zeal and an uncommon discernment and helped to establish the Orthodox faith; that he was afterwards chosen archbishop of Crete and much loved by the people; that **by prayer he drove the Saracens away from the island of Crete**; that the best known of his books, hymns and canons is the Great Canon of the Mother of God, „што се чита у четвртак пете недеље часнога поста“, read on the Thursday of the fifth week of the honourable fast; that his very look was such „да гледајући му лице и слушајући његове медоточне речи свак се наслађаваше и поправљаше“; and that returning once from Constantinople **he foretold his own death before he should reach Crete**, and so it happened. **AND THE TWO BOOKS PUT HIM ON OPPOSITE SIDES OF A SYNOD.** This book has him defend Orthodoxy against monothelitism at the Council of 681; saint.gr has him, as metropolitan, take part in the synod Bardanes convoked in 712 and there support Monophysitism, returning to the right faith after Bardanes’s death. **They are two different synods thirty-one years apart and the readings are not strictly in conflict**, which is exactly why neither is chosen and both are written. `types` UNTOUCHED: `hierarch` and `archbishop` are both there, „архиеп.“ is the `archbishop`; Свети is not a rank. **`wonderworker` AND `hymnographer` ARE REFUSED**: „Чињаше чудеса молитвама својим“ and the canons and hymns both stand in the **body**, where the heading gives only „архиеп.“, and a rank read off a body is not written — the fourth such refusal of this range. `office` UNTOUCHED at «Archbishop»: „Критски“ is the see and the display name carries it; no `office` string is invented. No `locations`: Damascus, Jerusalem, Constantinople, Crete and Mitylene in a narrative are not coordinates, and the folder has none. **NO NEW ROWS.** The folder already relates `germanus-of-constantinople`, `sergius-of-narva` and `therapon-of-cyprus`, and this book names none of them. **`sabbas-the-sanctified` takes no row**: the lavra is named after him and a dedication is not a relation — and the prose says «the lavra of Saint Sabbas» rather than his full name, because the first draft wrote „лавра св. Саве Освештаног“ out as «the lavra of Sabbas the Sanctified» and `related-floor.test.mjs` failed 484/1 on the reverse direction, `sabbas-the-sanctified -> andrew-of-crete`, that string being that folder’s display name exactly. **§6’s trap for the third time in this range**, after Isidore of Pelusium on 19 June and the pair on 2 July, and the first time it has caught a **monastery’s patron** rather than a person in the story: a dedication is not a relation, and a dedication written out in full is read as one. The fix was §6’s — the name out of the prose and into this note — applied as a `life_replace`-only spec, `.tmp/sr-drafts/fix-07-04.json`, with the same change made in the day’s generator, and this row then re-applied with `.tmp/sr-reapply-json.py`. Nothing was added to `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json`. **Theodore patriarch of Jerusalem takes no row**: he is named by rank and see and by a forename the corpus holds many times over, and an identification made off a name in another man’s life is not an identification. **Constantine the Bearded takes no row**, an emperor in a life not being automatically a relation. **The Saracens and the Council take none.** His parents George and Gregoria, whom doxologia names, are not in this book at all. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **THE DAY REFUSES NOBODY.** Both of its entries are persons, both are held, and both are upgrades — the first day of this range on which Ruling 3 has nothing to do. Nineteen days before this range had produced no new folder and four days in five had refused somebody; this is the fifth.

hymns.text: Îndreptătorule al Ortodoxiei, învăţătorule al dreptei cinstiri de Dumnezeu şi al curaţiei şi luminătorule al lumii, podoaba călugărilor cea de Dumnezeu insuflată Sfinte Ierarhe Andrei, înţelepte, cu învăţăturile tale pe toţi i-ai luminat. Alăută duhovnicească, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Andrei Ierusalimiteanul, Arhiepiscopul Cretei

english.text: Guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of the right worship of God and of purity, light of the world, God-inspired adornment of monks, wise hierarch Andrew: by your teachings you have given light to all. O spiritual lyre, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Κανόνα πίστεως, καὶ εἰκόνα πραότητος, ἐγκρατείας διδάσκαλον, ἀνέδειξε σε τῇ ποίμνῃ σου, ἡ τῶν πραγμάτων ἀλήθεια· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκτήσω τῇ ταπεινώσει τὰ ὑψηλά, τῇ πτωχείᾳ τὰ πλούσια. Πάτερ Ἱεράρχα Ἀνδρέα, πρέσβευε Χριστῷ τῷ θεῷ, σωθῆναι τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’ — the first of five apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Ανδρέας ο Ιεροσολυμίτης Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κρήτης»; it is the common of a hierarch, with his own name set into its last line

english.text: The truth of things has shown you to your flock as a rule of faith, an image of meekness and a teacher of self-restraint; therefore you have gained the heights by humility and riches by poverty. Father and hierarch Andrew, intercede with Christ our God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Σαλπίσας τρανῶς, τὰ θεῖα μελωδήματα, ἐδείχθης φωστήρ, τῷ κόσμῳ τηλαυγέστατος, τῷ φωτί λαμπόμενος, τῆς Τριάδος Ἀνδρέα Ὅσιε· ὅθεν πάντες βοῶμέν σοι, Μὴ παύσῃ πρεσβεύων ὑπὲρ πάντων ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — on the page of «Άγιος Ανδρέας ο Ιεροσολυμίτης Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κρήτης», and it names him

english.text: Sounding out the songs of God like a clear trumpet, you were shown to the world as a light seen from far off, shining with the light of the Trinity, O venerable Andrew. And so we all cry out to you: do not cease interceding for us all.
